replication.target_description: Li and Abarbanell (2018), Experiment 1 instructed conditions, percentage-correct ANOVA main effect of trial type (egocentric versus geocentric), across English/Tseltal children and both counterbalanced block orders. Matched by the named contrast and p.5 locator (printed p.13), not row ordering or statistic matching.

n.sample_role: Children contributing percentage-correct scores to the Experiment 1 instructed-condition ANOVA: 25 English-speaking and 32 Tseltal-speaking participants. Difficulty and trial type are repeated measures.
n.exclusions: Separate open-ended groups (14 English and 14 Tseltal) are outside this critical ANOVA. No further instructed-condition exclusions reported. Three Tseltal children not given the additional language-comprehension task are not excluded from this spatial analysis.
n.location: Printed p.14 (PDF p.6), Fig.2 caption; p.13 (PDF p.5), section 2.2.1.2; p.12, section 2.1.1.
n.quote: comparing the English (N = 25) and Tseltal speakers (N = 32).

notes: Only assigned n_r and reported_success completed. Original side and replication es/p are unassigned placeholders, not findings of absence. Analytic N derivation: 25 English-speaking + 32 Tseltal-speaking = 57 distinct children (Fig.2), mutually exclusive language groups in the instructed-condition analysis. Methods cross-check: English Ego-to-Geo 13 + Geo-to-Ego 12 = 25; Tseltal Ego-to-Geo 16 + Geo-to-Ego 16 = 32. Repeated egocentric/geocentric and easy/hard measurements are not summed. N is not inferred from df or whole-study recruitment. Reported success is mixed at the Experiment 1 replication-and-extension level: the authors say the replication portion mirrored Haun et al., while added manipulations did not favor the linguistic enculturation account. This is not a separate author verdict on each ANOVA main effect. The instructed-condition outcome is percentage correct, distinct from open-ended strategy classification. Rendered PDF pages 4–7 inspected for layout.
